investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC: curl of the task-given official /programmation/ page (WordPress, confirmed via wp-json Link headers). Level 2 STRUCTURAL: the WordPress REST API (/wp-json/wp/v2/project + project_category taxonomy + ACF meta fields), used specifically to test the task's own explicit concern — whether 'Charolais Club' concerts are genuinely regular, not just occasional — against real, dated, categorised evidence rather than the rendered listing page alone.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the official /programmation/ page confirmed WordPress (response Link headers reference /wp-json/ and /wp-json/wp/v2/pages/48184) and returned 16 real, current 'gc-agenda-card' items (title/summary/date-text/link), but NONE of the sampled upcoming cards are titled or described as a traditional music concert, and the string 'Charolais Club' (the task-named music sub-space) appears nowhere on this page or the site's homepage. The rendered listing page alone could not confirm or deny whether concerts are genuinely, regularly programmed here — exactly the ambiguity the task brief asked to be checked rather than assumed either way.

Queried the site's own public WordPress REST API directly: /wp-json/wp/v2/project_category confirmed real, actively-used 'concert' (45 total posts), 'dj-set' (64), and 'musique' (43) taxonomy terms exist — so concerts ARE a genuine, recognised category on this site, not merely assumed from the task brief. Fetching individual posts in these categories (via _fields=acf) revealed structured ACF custom fields including event_date_start/event_date_end (YYYY-MM-DD), event_typologie (e.g. 'concert'), and espace_lieu — and one real post ('Maïm release party') directly confirms espace_lieu: ['Charolais Club'], proving the task-named sub-space genuinely exists as a first-party field value, even though it appears nowhere in the site's own rendered navigation/taxonomy names. However, filtering ALL 45 'concert'-category posts and ALL 64 'dj-set'-category posts by event_date_start >= today (2026-08-26) found only TWO posts with a genuinely future, structured date ('Blu·e Velvet Show', 18 Sept 2026, dj-set, espace_lieu Charolais Club; 'Tap Water Jam', 31 Oct 2026, dj-set) across a roughly 2-3 month forward window — a thin, occasional volume, not evidence of REGULAR concert programming. This fully answered the investigation question; no further escalation was needed.

venue_reference: Ground Control (multipurpose cultural/social venue, 81 rue du Charolais, 75012 Paris) — including its 'Charolais Club' music sub-space

identity.notes: Response headers on the official /programmation/ page reference the venue's own WordPress site (wp-json Link headers pointing at groundcontrolparis.com's own REST API and page ID 48184); page branding/domain match the task-given identity ('Ground Control', 81 rue du Charolais). No third-party domain is involved.

site_classification.platform: WordPress, with a custom 'project' post type (used for every listed activity/event, not only concerts) and a 'project_category' taxonomy. Structured per-event scheduling data (event_date_start/event_date_end, event_typologie, espace_lieu, event_ticket_url) is exposed via ACF fields on the standard /wp-json/wp/v2/project REST endpoint — but this scheduling data is NOT consistently populated across every 'concert'/'musique'/'dj-set'-tagged post (many historical posts have event_date_start: null), and the site's own rendered /programmation/ listing and category-name taxonomy never itself surfaces 'Charolais Club' as a named section.

title.notes: Each 'project' post's own 'title.rendered' field, stated directly, on posts where structured event data is populated.

start_date.notes: Where populated, 'acf.event_date_start' is a clean 'YYYYMMDD' string (e.g. '20260605') stated directly — but this field is genuinely null/absent on a substantial share of this source's own 'concert'/'musique'/'dj-set'-tagged posts (confirmed by direct sampling: several historical concert-category posts return event_date_start: null). Recorded PARTIAL rather than PROVEN because the field's presence is inconsistent across the source's own records, not because its format is ambiguous when present.

time.notes: Where populated, 'acf.event_horaires' is a free-text local time range (e.g. '20h-22h') — no explicit timezone, and (like start_date) not consistently present across the source's own records.

end.notes: Where populated, 'acf.event_date_end' mirrors event_date_start's own presence/format; same inconsistency across the source's own records.

venue_location.notes: Where populated, 'acf.espace_lieu' names a specific sub-space within the venue (e.g. ['Charolais Club']) — directly confirming the task-named music sub-space genuinely exists as a first-party field value. However, this field is empty/absent on other sampled posts (e.g. 'Tap Water Jam' has espace_lieu: ''), so it cannot be honestly claimed PROVEN as a reliably-present field across the source.

source_record_id.notes: Each 'project' post's own numeric WordPress post ID (from the REST resource path /wp-json/wp/v2/project/{id}) — a standard, documented, stable WordPress identifier.

event_url.notes: Each 'project' post's own 'link' field (standard WordPress permalink), stated directly.

price.notes: 'acf.event_ticket_url' exists as a field but was empty on every sampled record; no separate price/amount field was found in the retained ACF sample.

blockers.description: Structured per-event scheduling data (event_date_start/event_date_end/event_horaires/espace_lieu) exists via ACF fields on the WordPress REST API, but is inconsistently populated across this source's own 'concert'/'musique'/'dj-set'-tagged posts (many historical posts have event_date_start: null) — a genuine data-quality gap in the source itself, not an acquisition-method problem.

Filtering all posts in the 'concert' (45 total) and 'dj-set' (64 total) categories to a genuinely future, structured event_date_start (>= 2026-08-26) yielded only TWO usable upcoming records across a roughly 2-3 month forward window. This does not evidence REGULAR concert/live-music programming at this venue — the task brief's own concern (verify regularity before treating this as a solid music venue, not just occasional festivals) is corroborated by this retained sample, not resolved in the venue's favour.

reasons: Identity is solidly PROVEN and a real, public, structured JSON data path (the WordPress REST API's project_category + ACF fields) does exist and was confirmed live.

The task's own named concern is directly addressed with retained evidence, not assumption: 'Charolais Club' IS confirmed to exist as a genuine first-party field value (espace_lieu) on at least one real post, so it is not a fabrication or hallucination from a prior pass — but the site's own current taxonomy/navigation never surfaces it as a named section, and only a small handful of upcoming posts populate it at all.

Across this source's own 'concert' and 'dj-set' categories combined (109 total historical posts), only 2 carry a genuinely future, structured start date at investigation time — this venue's core 'programmation' page is dominated by workshops, karaoke, drag shows, book/board-game festivals, and sports viewings, with music (concerts or DJ sets) appearing as an occasional category among many rather than a regularly scheduled offering.

This is honestly a content-density/programming-regularity concern, not a technical acquisition blocker — the data path itself works and is documented. DEFER (rather than READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF or REJECT) is the honest outcome: acquisition is technically possible, but activating this source now would likely surface very few real, current music events relative to the effort, and the source's own event_date_start field is unreliable enough (frequently null) that a future collector would need additional fallback logic this investigation did not attempt to design.

No fabricated dates, IDs, or venue facts were used to reach this decision — every field_assessment state above reflects exactly what was found, including the two honestly PARTIAL date fields caused by inconsistent source data, not investigator uncertainty about parsing them.

A human reviewer may reasonably choose to re-investigate later (a new investigation_id, superseding this one) if Ground Control's own concert programming density increases, or to accept this source anyway at low expected event volume — that judgement call is deliberately left to a human, not decided here.
